questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please pass _________ the salt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this sentence, the preposition “pass” requires an object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them) to indicate the person receiving the action.
 
• Among the given options, **“me”** is the correct object pronoun to use after “pass.”
 
• The sentence therefore becomes grammatically correct and meaningful as “Please pass **me** the salt.”
 
• Options like “my,” “mine,” or “I” are incorrect because they are possessive or subject pronouns, not object pronouns.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“Please pass **me** the salt.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **“My”** – a possessive adjective, used before nouns (e.g., my book).
 
• **“Mine”** – a possessive pronoun, used without a noun (e.g., This book is mine).
 
• **“I”** – a subject pronoun, used before verbs (e.g., I am reading).
 
• **“Me”** – an object pronoun, used after verbs or prepositions (e.g., Pass me the salt).

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form. I shall come again in the afternoon for lunch.

options.text: I will be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
I shall have come again in the afternoon for lunch
I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
I will come again in the afternoon for lunch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question asks us to express the sentence in the **future continuous tense.**
 
• The **future continuous tense** is used to indicate actions that will be ongoing at a particular time in the future.
 
• The structure of the future continuous tense is: **Subject + shall/will + be + present participle (verb+ing).**
 
• The given sentence is: *"I shall come again in the afternoon for lunch."*
 
• In the future continuous tense, this will become: **I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.**

Correct sentence: *I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + will/shall + be + verb (ing).
 
• **Example:** She will be reading a book at 5 PM tomorrow.
 
• **Usage: **To describe actions that will be ongoing at a specific time in the future.
 
 
 
• **Other Tenses:**
 
 
• **Simple Future:** I will come again in the afternoon.
 
• **Future Perfect:** I shall have come again in the afternoon.
